h1: La Flora Khao Lak — a beachfront resort on Bang Niang within walking distance of both the sand and the night market
intro: If you want a Khao Lak resort where you wake up to the sea but can still stroll out to grab dinner at the night market, La Flora Khao Lak is the answer many travellers land on. This 4-star beachfront resort on Bang Niang Beach has 154 rooms scattered through tropical gardens, two lagoon pools and pool-access rooms you step straight into from the terrace. Open since 2005 and kept up well enough to earn a 9.6 from 77 Trip.com reviews. From approx. ฿3,500/night.

body.html: La Flora Khao Lak has been open since 2005 and is one of the resorts Khao Lak regulars know well. What draws people here is the direct frontage onto Bang Niang Beach — step out of the resort and you are on the sand facing the Andaman Sea, while a few minutes' walk takes you to Bang Niang Road with its restaurants, massage shops and night market. The 154 rooms sit in low-rise buildings spread through tropical gardens rather than one tall block, which makes the place feel leafier and more private than you might expect.

Rooms start with the Deluxe Room at around 42 sq m in the garden buildings. Step up to a Pool Access Room of about 45 sq m, where the terrace doors open straight onto the lagoon pool — the room type guests talk about most, because it is only a few steps from bed to water. Seaside Pool Access rooms sit in the Seaside Wing nearest the beach, and the Flora 2-Bedroom suits families or groups. Guests praise the spacious, clean rooms, comfortable beds and usable terraces, though some note the older garden-wing rooms feel more dated than the seaside ones.
"We booked a pool-access room — opened the doors in the morning and slid straight into the pool, then in the evening walked a few steps out to watch the sunset on Bang Niang Beach. Brilliant value."

The heart of the resort is its two lagoon pools winding through the gardens and linking to the pool-access wing. The beachside Sire restaurant serves Thai and international food with a sea view, while the Floranica Spa and fitness centre cover the quieter days. There is a kids' club and a separate children's pool, which makes this an easy choice for families. The breakfast buffet earns regular praise for its range of Thai and Western options, though several guests flag that food and drink prices inside the resort run noticeably higher than the restaurants just outside.

To be honest, La Flora has a few trade-offs to weigh. The one guests mention most is that poolside sunbeds get claimed early in the morning, so in high season a late riser can struggle to find a spot by the water. Some reviews note the in-resort food prices, and that older garden-wing rooms are worth asking about — request a renovated room if you can. The location is also about an hour by road from Phuket airport, and Bang Niang Beach turns shallow and wide at low tide like most of the Khao Lak coast. It scores 9.6 from 77 Trip.com reviews and 4.6/5 from over 920 TripAdvisor reviews (#27 in Khao Lak) — consistently well regarded.

La Flora Khao Lak is best for travellers who want a beachfront resort at an approachable price and like being able to walk out for food. Families with kids, couples after a pool-access room, or anyone who wants to stay by the sea without paying luxury rates will be well served here. If you are set on deep swimming all day or want a brand-new design resort, look at the other options in this roundup. Rates start around ฿3,500/night in low season and climb to ฿6,000–8,000+ in high season for pool-access and seaside rooms.

A tip from following the reviews here: if the budget stretches, choose a Pool Access or Seaside Pool Access room so you can slip into the pool from your terrace and sit closer to the beach — better value than the garden-wing Deluxe, which is a longer walk. Grab a poolside sunbed early if you travel in high season, and walk out to the Bang Niang night market for at least one dinner, since in-resort prices are higher and the street food is right there.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — La Flora Khao Lak, Phang Nga

faq.q: Where is La Flora Khao Lak and how do I get there?
faq.a: La Flora Khao Lak sits on Bang Niang Beach in Khuk Khak, Takua Pa District, Phang Nga. It is about an hour by road from Phuket International Airport (HKT), and roughly a 5-minute walk to the Bang Niang night market and restaurant street. The resort can arrange transfers, but compare the price against a Grab or taxi first.

faq.q: How much does La Flora Khao Lak cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start around ฿3,500/night for a Deluxe Room (~42 sq m, garden wing). Step up to a Pool Access Room (~45 sq m, pool from the terrace), Seaside Pool Access (nearest the beach) or the Flora 2-Bedroom for families. In high season rates climb to ฿6,000–8,000+. Always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does La Flora Khao Lak have rooms with direct pool access?
faq.a: Yes — the Pool Access and Seaside Pool Access rooms open straight onto the lagoon pool from the terrace. They are the most talked-about room type because it is only a few steps from bed to water, ideal for couples and families who want easy swimming.

faq.q: Is La Flora Khao Lak good for families?
faq.a: Very much so. The resort has a kids' club, a separate children's pool, Flora 2-Bedroom suites and a varied breakfast buffet with Thai and Western dishes. The low-rise garden layout is easy for kids to wander safely, and the shallow beach at low tide is good for sandcastles.

faq.q: Can you swim at the beach in front of La Flora Khao Lak?
faq.a: Bang Niang Beach in front of the resort is swimmable depending on the tide, like most of the Khao Lak coast. At low tide it turns shallow and wide, better for strolling and for kids playing on the sand, so most guests use the resort's lagoon pools as well. The beach is a lovely sunset spot.

faq.q: Is food expensive at La Flora Khao Lak?
faq.a: Some reviews note that food and drink prices inside the resort run noticeably higher than outside. The upside is that the Bang Niang night market and restaurant street are only a few minutes' walk away and far cheaper. A good plan is breakfast at the resort buffet, then walk out for dinner to save.
